question.problem:
Solve the modular equation $9x≡8\,(\text{mod}\,14),$ expressing your answer as a nonnegative integer smaller than $14.$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*

$x≡$
{{field-1}}$\,(\text{mod}\,14)$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=9$ and $n=14$, where

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(9,14)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $9\,(\text{mod}\,14).$ To find the inverse of $9\,(\text{mod}\,14)$, we compute the exponents of $9\,(\text{mod}\,14)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,14):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{9}^{2} & ≡81≡11 &  & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ {9}^{3} & ≡11\cdot 9≡99≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,14)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $11\cdot 9≡1\,(\text{mod}\,14),$ which means that $11$ is the multiplicative inverse of $9$ (modulo $14$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $11,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}9x & ≡8 &  & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ 11\cdot 9x & ≡11\cdot 8 &  & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ (11\cdot 9)x & ≡88 &  & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡4+6\cdot 14 &  & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ x & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,14)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,14).$
